claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as having poor performance, stuttering, and frametime spikes.

citations.review_text:
Great game, lot of fun with friends.

Optimization leaves to be desired. Wild stuttering and frametime spikes.

Definitely worth on sale. It is good fun, the combat and skill tree/build depth is great, the atmosphere is awesome and the sound/visuals all good. You sprint through the level so it can be hard to appreciate the detail. There are some seriously god awful UI design choices, but its whatever. The monetization is disgusting, typical for Fatshark though.

The biggest issue I have is constant crashing and horrendous performance. Many changes and adjustments are needed to run this game at all.

claims.claim: Reviewers report frequent crashes and unstable performance during missions.

citations.review_text:
This game and this game specifically crashes all the time. I've gone less than a minute between crashes. Every fix that I can find and try makes the game less stable.
The tutorial seemed fine. The lobby is often fine, other than the horrendous input lag.
Thankfully, the input lag goes away in actual missions... when the game is actually running and not crashing so hard it takes every monitor with it.

Definitely worth on sale. It is good fun, the combat and skill tree/build depth is great, the atmosphere is awesome and the sound/visuals all good. You sprint through the level so it can be hard to appreciate the detail. There are some seriously god awful UI design choices, but its whatever. The monetization is disgusting, typical for Fatshark though.

The biggest issue I have is constant crashing and horrendous performance. Many changes and adjustments are needed to run this game at all.

[h1]Not Recommended[/h1]

[b]Almost four years after launch, Darktide still has the same problems it had on day one.[/b]

[h2]The Good[/h2]
[list]
[*]Looks great and nails the grimdark 40K atmosphere
[*]The first few missions are genuinely fun
[/list]

[h2]The Bad[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Repetitive progression:[/b] The game seems to only open up around level 20, and getting there is a long, monotonous slog.
[*][b]Matchmaking:[/b] It's unreliable enough that much of that early grind ends up solo, which isn't what a co-op game should feel like.
[*][b]Stability:[/b] Frequent crashes, even on a system with 64GB of RAM. That shouldn't happen this long after release.
[*][b]Maps and missions:[/b] Little variety. The same environments and objectives repeat quickly.
[*][b]Combat:[/b] Feels more like button-mashing and spam than skill-based melee.
[/list]

[h2]Verdict[/h2]
The setting and visuals promise a lot, but the core loop doesn't deliver. Until the crashes, matchmaking and repetitive content are fixed, it's hard to recommend, especially at full price. Wait for a sale or a major overhaul.

[b]Score: 4/10[/b]

claims.claim: Reviewers find the upgrade menus and user interface confusing and overly complicated for new players.

citations.review_text: It's Left 4 Dead but as humans in 40K. It looks great and plays well but some of the mechanics are confusing & poorly explained (especially the levelling-up stuff) although you can certainly find fan guides for everything. Never had a problem finding humans to play with; start your mission and while you might play the first few minutes with bots, people will show up once the thing is live. Objective locations can be confusing but the levels aren't very big. The game encourages you to stick together. Demands a powerful PC to run at peak (mine is probably underspec for CPU but my GPU isn't half bad). Looking forward to levelling up the base classes and then trying some DLC ones.
It's fun. But why are there so many sub menus to upgrade stuff? What is this? It's so confusing when you're new to the game. The performance is trash. Fix your game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game suffers from poor optimization, causing low and inconsistent frame rates that require aggressive upscaling or configuration adjustments to manage.

citations.review_text: Half of my "game time" so far has been in the ini file trying to - 1. stop crashing and 2. actually achieve consistantly playable frame rates. Bro its not like a have a shoddy pc or anything, its actually pretty decent but this game doesent care about that one bit. visuals are fantastic though, its real trip if you like 40K. Just wish they didnt shoe horn in DX12 and ray tracing into an engine that didnt originally support it. feel like it ruined the potential performance consistancy. which really hurts the gameplay. I didnt pay thousands for a pc setup only to have my games run at 45 fps then 150 fps then 45 fps again its all over the shop. Heard vermintide 2 has none of that, performance supposed to be spot on. Shoulda did that but 40k skinned. Overall, If Darktide is on sale and you like 40k and/or horde shooters, its worth it for the setting/visuals alone. if you dont care for 40k and like horde shooters just get deep rock galactic, doesent even matter if its on sale just get it. This game took clear inspiration for DRG and for good reason its an awesome game.

Good game with nice gunplay and unique characters builds. Environments are a cool backdrop. Too bad the performance is straight garbage. 

With an RTX 3060 and a Ryzen 3700X, I get 40 fps at most in the LOWEST graphics at 1440p. DLSS is mandatory for the best image quality because this game is dependent on Temporal Anti-Aliasing which makes the game extremely blurry with artifacting. 

Not only is DLSS mandatory, DLSS Performance Mode or 50% resolution scaling is the only way to get 60fps on average with dips to 40-50fps. Could brute force more performance with Ultra-Performance Mode with a 33% resolution scaling because DLSS has a good enough image quality. But that's embarrassingly below the resolution of the PS3 and Xbox 360.

A bit of tough luck if you have an RTX 2000 series card because the new Transformer DLSS is not as performant compared to on RTX 3000 series and later. If you don't have an Nvidia RTX card, XESS 2 is a pretty good alternative that works on modern graphics cards, though you will need to use a DLSS Swapper to switch from XESS 1 to 2. No clue about FSR4, but FSR1 to 3 are pretty terrible (less so on FSR3 but it's not as stable as XESS).

Really embarrassing for a game (most modern games to be fair) to require you to play at Ultra Performance which is equal or below the Playstation 2 resolution at 480p or 360p if your monitor is 1440p or 1080p respectively.
Good alternative for L4D2 fans. Only thing that is that perrformance is absolutely atrocious. I have to use 720p to 4k upscale on medium settings to hit 80-120 fps on rtx 3090. Insane.

The game is great fun! Shooting feels fantastic, melee feels powerful, enemies have great variety and great pathfinding, character banter is great, visuals are gorgeous, sound design is memorable, music makes you bob your head the moment it kicks in. Buy it on sale at 80-90% off!

Now here's why I don't recommend buying it for full price:
1. On my 2080S I was getting 20-30FPS on the lowest settings at 1080p and ultra performance DLSS 4.0 when I started playing the game. Why? The game doesn't actually turn off raytraced lighting in the config file, it stays on High, I found that out thanks to a YouTube video. Editing the config file directly made me get to more or less stable 60 at 1440p with Balanced DLSS preset and most settings maxed out. Question is, how the FUCK is this a known issue 4 years after game's release?
2. Game suffers from massive performance issues between different menus. Opening 2D mastery window can suddenly tank your framerate to 20s for no reason. Why? I dunno, ask Fatshark.
3. Darktide also suffers from a KNOWN memory leak that will randomly and permanently drop your frames until you restart the game. Apparently it was introduced by Skitarii class update this June. That was 4 months ago, very cool.
4. Remember how you could set up any bots you want in Vermintide? And change their gear to things you own? Well you can't do it here. You want to do a slow exploration run alone or in co-op with your friend? Enjoy your unranked veterans with basic starting weapons. Bots are also somehow even dumber than in Vermintide, sometimes they can just get stuck in the elevators, ignore area hazards, fall down ledges or refuse to revive players nearby. Bots aren't just bad, they're a genuine liability that can ruin the run for you.
5. Female character creator is a joke. Listen, I get it, you can't have perfect skin on a diet of corpse starch and reused service water. But why does every female face in the game look either like a hag who's been chain smoking and …

claims.claim: Reviewers report a lack of mission variety and note that available missions feel repetitive.

citations.review_text:
Great game with great characters and fun gameplay. The only things holding it back are the small number of missions and the lack of a proper endless endgame mode.

A lot of people mention technical issues, and while it could definitely be better optimized. I haven't run into anything major myself. Also, I love 40K so I automatically love this game.

I played all classes (except for the Skitarii) and I can confidently say that the gameplay loop is extremely repetitive and uninteresting. The maps and missions are essentially the same. A lot of special enemies are pointless and/or are not fun to engage with, like tox bombers, the two types of flamer enemies, etc. The game feels like a cheap copy of Left4Dead, where the special enemies don't have such a clear role.

Getting caught by a net when multiple enemies are essentially clipped together is not fun. It is also required that a second player or bot has to physically interact with the net to get you out. A horde of bullet sponge enemies like Crushers and Maulers is so unfun to deal with. Add boss enemies into the mix together with tox bombers and flamers and you get an artificially difficult, unfun mess of an experience. To make things worse, the character customization is lackluster and the cosmetics are very expensive. If you want a specific cosmetic, you can't outright buy it, you have to wait for it to become available on the in-game store. 

I haven't played Havoc 40, so I won't comment on it. But I have to admit that I really like the build variety and complexity. The toughness system works really well and I quite like it, but that's about it for the positives.

Overall, it's just a bland horde shooter. Only play this if you're a huge 40K fan,

claims.claim: Reviewers report that certain graphics cards, specifically AMD models, experience consistent crashing and technical instability that makes the game unplayable.

citations.review_text:
As of right now 11-12-2026, there is an issue after the Arcane Ruin update with AMD 7000 series graphics cards.

The game crashes consistently without failure during any mission or game mode on this series of card. Until the issue is fixed I can't recommend this game to anyone that has this series or possibly even any AMD brand of card.

If you don't have one of these cards I highly recommend the game if you like Vermintide, or hoard shooters in general. Every class from the base 4 and DLC classes so far have been extremely fun. Guns, melee, and movement all feels very responsive while the skill trees lets you have a variety of build options.

This is what truly pains me the most about having to leave this review. Until the issue is fixed I can't play my current favorite game to grind and enjoy. If it comes out that this is an AMD issue then I will change or make an update to this review, but for now I refuse to change it unless something gets fixed.

AMD GPUs keep your distance!

Played this a lot back when I was still running a system with an NVidia GPU. Upgraded to an AMD one a while back, game has been UNPLAYABLE since then. Constant crashes, mostly cannot even finish one mission, even on potato settings. All the "helpful troubleshooting tips" and "workarounds" Fatshark offers help exactly not at all.

It has litterally been years now. I've given up on this.

Like the Game, HATE the Graphics Support. i like this game a lot more than Vermintide. Ive been playing it a lot. the game play loop is a big adrenalin rush once you get into a flow. its a "Get Good" kind of difficulty curve at higher play levers.

HOWEVER!! theres been a huge support outage with the Radeon 7800 series Graphics cards and the game will hang/crash if you have this kind of card.  apparently this has happened with this game and this graphics arrangement it the past and has been fixed before but it appears to be a frequent problem with this range of Graphics cards.

My game is currently unplayable unless i roll my Drivers back to such an old state that none of my other games long using them.  and that does not even fix the crashing it only lessens it.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game suffers from frequent disconnects, server instability, and connection issues during missions.

citations.review_text: Great co-op game and super addicting to play with others. I normally wouldn't play a game like this on my own, but this one is fire! Just wish they would fix the constant disconnects (happens 3-4 times a mission for me). Overall, highly recommend.

I've come to the conclusion that Swedish game developers have an uncanny talent for making initially excellent games, but having said games contain a massive can of worms when you look under the hood. 

In terms of performance, Darktide is notoriously bad and easily prone to crashing and connectivity issues. Visually the game can have stunning environments but the engine is chugging at its very limits and heavily relying on DLSS to function. 

In terms of gameplay, the core gameplay loop is very entertaining, but can be set back by other aspects of the game, such as the necessity for meta builds in higher difficulties, class balance issues and some weapons being objectively bad compared to everything else. 
 The base game contains four classes - The Ogryn, Veteran, Psyker and Zealot. The DLCs add The Hive Scum, Arbite and Skitarii. Two of the core problems with the DLC classes are a serious lack of synergy with other classes and their pricetags. Other problems range from lacking weapon variety or being generally underwhelming, such as the Hive Scum in particular having to get reworked multiple times over time to make it feasible. 
 As for the base classes, they do synergize well with each other, but still suffer from clear balance issues when you're playing in higher difficulties, where specific skills and attributes are objectively more favorable than others, and certain classes vastly outperforming the others. 
 To elaborate, The Ogryn class is the class that struggles the most in higher difficulties. The class with the largest health pool in the game, also has a passive ability to draw majority of attention by the enemy AI, which increase in number in greater difficulties, causing his health pool to melt in scenarios with lots of ranged enemies too far for the Ogryn to get within melee distance. Ogryn, as a class is far more focused in melee combat rather than ranged, and despite having range-focused skills and abilities available in his skill tree, they are cons…
I’m absolutely fed up with the constant bugs, crashes, and disconnects.

claims.claim: Reviewers report frequent crashes, connectivity issues, and performance instability, specifically noting problems affecting AMD graphics card users.

citations.review_text:
As of right now 11-12-2026, there is an issue after the Arcane Ruin update with AMD 7000 series graphics cards.

The game crashes consistently without failure during any mission or game mode on this series of card. Until the issue is fixed I can't recommend this game to anyone that has this series or possibly even any AMD brand of card.

If you don't have one of these cards I highly recommend the game if you like Vermintide, or hoard shooters in general. Every class from the base 4 and DLC classes so far have been extremely fun. Guns, melee, and movement all feels very responsive while the skill trees lets you have a variety of build options.

This is what truly pains me the most about having to leave this review. Until the issue is fixed I can't play my current favorite game to grind and enjoy. If it comes out that this is an AMD issue then I will change or make an update to this review, but for now I refuse to change it unless something gets fixed.

AMD GPUs keep your distance!

Played this a lot back when I was still running a system with an NVidia GPU. Upgraded to an AMD one a while back, game has been UNPLAYABLE since then. Constant crashes, mostly cannot even finish one mission, even on potato settings. All the "helpful troubleshooting tips" and "workarounds" Fatshark offers help exactly not at all.

It has litterally been years now. I've given up on this.

Like the Game, HATE the Graphics Support. i like this game a lot more than Vermintide. Ive been playing it a lot. the game play loop is a big adrenalin rush once you get into a flow. its a "Get Good" kind of difficulty curve at higher play levers.

HOWEVER!! theres been a huge support outage with the Radeon 7800 series Graphics cards and the game will hang/crash if you have this kind of card.  apparently this has happened with this game and this graphics arrangement it the past and has been fixed before but it appears to be a frequent problem with this range of Graphics cards.

My game is currently unplayable unless i roll my Drivers back to such an old state that none of my other games long using them.  and that does not even fix the crashing it only lessens it. 

im frustrated because i really do like this game a lot. and was playing it non stop for months before this hotfix bricked the game for me. its a really mixed bag.

Good game, but networking issues makes it hard to play, even with a fiber connection and a 5070TI.

A great hord killing game with lots of mods available on Nexus Mods for things like better scoreboards and other quality of life features.  As with all mods, each time the game gets a major update they break, but the modding community usually gets them back up and running quickly.

4 Base Classes, with 2 DLC classes, maximum 4 players per team.
Main game modes come with multiple difficulties, different maps, objectives.
Havoc table offers some added weight to fighting through.
Psychanium offers 12 round events with random special skills being added to your class' base skills, gear & tools.
Campaign mode contains larger maps, limited resources, and different objective types from the main game modes.
Additionally there periodically are special events to achieve individual wins and global wins.

Plenty of audio cues for the specials including; Demon Hosts, Trappers, Bursters, Hounds, Snipers, Mutants, and more.

Very robust, however sometimes long loading times or disconnect issues, and 100% necessary to run on an SSD.  Really can't recommend this more as a previous player of Vermintide 2, this offers a new taste to the Warhammer horde killing gaming community whether your preference is for 40K lore or for vermin.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as featuring diverse melee and ranged weapon mechanics, distinct class skill trees, and responsive movement options like sliding and dodging.

citations.review_text:
This game takes everything I loved about the left 4 dead games and improves, along with adding more. The characters all not only play meaningfully different from one another, but they also have different builds that play meaningfully different from one another. Every character different enough with enough variation within to make you want to try a bunch of different builds out, and as with all great games, the true endgame is fashion. And even though it takes a sec to start earning the good ones, there are some great free cosmetics. 

I have way too much I can compliment about darktide, but they all come together when one enemy spawns, the Poxburster. You'll be in the middle of clearing a fresh horde, the absolutely phenomenal music is going nuclear, and you're doing your aoe melee combo. Then you hear the sound cue for the burster, perfectly designed to cut through all of the other noise, and your options are to either lose most or all of your health or to lock in and shove the burster away at the right time. There is no other game I've ever played that has me trained the way darktide does, I feel like if I heard that sound in public I'd go into fight or flight.

The main thing that every new player should know is to STAY WITH YOPIR TEAM. This game does punish you for being a lone wolf until you're skilled enough to not get caught off guard by the specialist enemies, which once you have it down is very easy since every specialist enemy has its own solution. You just need to build the muscle memory. With some good headphones you can deal with most specialists on sound cues alone, and it will make you feel incredible. 

Last bit is the warhammer stuff. I am only a lore consumer, read a couple books and played some of the videogames. If you have no idea about warhammer, it really just feels like a dark dystopian scifi world with demons and wicked art design. If you know just a little bit about warhammer like myself, it absolutely makes everything a bit cooler. …

If you've never played a Tide game before, the simplest way to distill it is that at its core, it is a L4D style game. Coop, 4 person, dropped into missions -- kill things, fulfill some straightforward objectives, occasionally kill a boss or two, leave, repeat ad infimum. 

That being said, Darktide is quite a bit more under the hood. It is a true mishmash of a lot of game genres. The combat is not just shooting things with guns (though all the guns are very unique, varied and are great) but also very intertwined with a melee system that boasts precise hitboxes, a stamina system, blocking, pushing, and even sometimes parrying. Characters also have i-frame dodges, and melee weapons across all the different classes also have specific movesets with specific strengths and weaknesses. You can almost call it a soulslike in some fashion, right down to some of the encounters even becoming quite challenging once you're deep enough in the difficulty slider. 

Speaking of, there are character classes, and each class is very distinct in role, feel, and overall play. All classes have unique weapons, talent trees, and abilities, and all serve something different, so the RPG aspect is even there. There is character creation, and the voice acting is actually a shining gem in this game and is very entertaining and very well done. Banter between the characters never gets old and there is actually SO MUCH varied dialogue. There's kind of a story, but its vague and not told or presented very well. But the lore is quite dense and rich if you're willing to dig a bit or watch a video or two. 

To be clear, this game isn't perfect. The performance is still not great (though leagues better than it once was at launch) and it stutters and bugs out sometime. It is amusingly, yet another, pseudo live-service game built on the spaghetti coded backbone of the Autodesk Stingray, and is run by a Swedish dev that are gun nerds. (Yes this is exactly what Helldivers 2 is). On the subject of the live s…

An immersive marvel.

Darktide is by all means a great game.
At first glance, it might not look like there's much to it but hacking away, especially from gameplay videos on Youtube. But you have to dive into it, to learn what's great about the combat flow.
Without being PvP, this game manages to be some of the most intense action at a very fast pace.
With sliding being the best way to dodge ranged fire, and dodging or blocking the way to negate melee harm. Block+attack to push being just short of a necessary move too. 
Melee weapons having each their own damage values and swing patterns that matter. Certain moves being able to be block-cancelled for optimal horde clearing or damaging big targets.
All this comes together, to create incredibly engaging combat, that feels rewarding to master in a way that can't be described. And that's just melee combat.
Then factor in, abilities, blitzes and perk interactions. You have a ranged weapon too. 
You just have to feel it for yourself.

Slap onto that an incredible environmental design and a soundtrack that's honestly one of gaming history's finest.
The cast of characters that surround your squad are phenomenal and memorable, which is why I'm not buying the argument, that Vermintide's playable characters having so much personality, is an area where this game falters.
You're getting that sort of "named character" banter from the cast like Hadron and Rannick. Then the personalities of the player characters provide a more befitting motley crew feeling for the action banner. This, in my opinion, honestly works better.
The player characters do have a set character, but with enough room to make it feel like your own character. Thus, forming better immersion and a sense of agency.

The missions have a good length, and there are currently just enough, to with the balance of build variety, make it avoid being too repetitive.
Add onto this, the fact that difficulty upticks actually feel meaningful, with a bonus, ranke…

Game is 9/10 and it's so underrated, the content, weapons, classes, builds, bosses, enemies, maps, It's just very good, you should definitely buy it. It's innovative and fun, I can appreciate the devs have put tons of effort and love towards this game.

Now, there are a couple of things that I wish could be better, such as performance, certain mobs like the trapper and poxburster not making noise when they're supposed to and catching you off guard (you eventually get used to dodging it but it's still annoying), these could all improve much more.

That being said, this is one of my favourite games of all time.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the cash shop as heavily driven by fear-of-missing-out tactics and place certain desirable cosmetics behind paywalls.

citations.review_text: This game does what every other new title does... They put time limited items that are no longer redeemable or viewable. Why not cycle the entire inventory like Halo MCC to further the accessibility to cosmetic variety? This game is about personal builds and play styles. Why kick your own feet out gatekeeping. I'm specifically referring to Portrait Frames and Icons (they don't have monetary value). They've done ok with cycling the commadores' vestures (paid cosmetics). I played the Daemon Host event and no frame was given. Make it available some other way! The previous event frames and icons blow the earned ones out of the water! F.O.M.O. is Fake and Gay. Give Equal/Full Access!

Probably THE best Horde Coop game out there. 

Music thanks to Jesper Kyd is a straight 11/10
The combat combined with the Movement feels super meaty, crunchy and smooth, especially if you learn all the little quirks of the movement! (Put Crouch and Dodge on the same button, put jump on a seperate button, trust me)
ALL Classes are amazing, even if you dont wanna get the dlc classes instantly when buying the game, you will have 4 amazing classes to level, tons of builds to try and alot of weapon masteries to level. The Penances give some pretty cool cosmetics for all 4 Base classes. Also every Weapon has a Mastery Skin.

This game isnt without its problems tho, i wish haha.
Perfomance, depending on your system, can be very hit or miss. I would consider my pc pretty powerful but without tweaking ini files, Instant Mourningstar Mod and Quickload Missions mod, it can get pretty wonky sometimes. AMD users are hit by this the most as far as i know. BUT there are a ton of Guides out there that can really help mitigate these problems. Also the Cash Shop for Cosmetics is the biggest FOMO S*** Show ever. I dont mind the cosmetic shop because i dont care about it, but it might be dealbreaker for some out there.

SO, overall, this is one of the best Horde Shooters i have ever played. The Basic Combat Loop is so addicting that i can overlook the problems this game has. Its "Skill Expression- The Game"

FATSHARK, PLEASE FIX THE PERFOMANCE OF THIS OTHERWISE AMAZING GAME!

9/10

It's a really fun game with lots of verity in terms of how you can play, it's a great game if you like killing hoards.

Psyker is my favourite class in the game as you can use the purgaratus staff with brain burst and it's quite fun to do so in havoc, I would just say watch out for Daemonhost while you do so.

The cosmetics are really good I just wish most of the really nice ones such as the steel legion, Death Korps, Vostryoans and such weren't behind a paywall, and that you didn't have to wait for a lucky roll in the shop to get the cosmetics you want.

The penances are a nice thing to work towards, some of them are easier to do with help otherwise they're quite annoying to do, but most of them you'll be able to get just by playing, so I wouldn't worry about the others until you want to, or if you even want to do them.

10/10 would recommend getting thrown off by a barrel again
